html:
The steelpan is a drum made from an oil barrel, hammered so that each part sounds a different note. It was invented in the poor districts of Port of Spain in the late 1930s and 1940s.

Colonial rulers had banned skin drums, so Carnival bands beat bamboo, then tins and dustbins. Young men found that dented steel gave tuned notes, and the 55 gallon oil drums of the island's oil industry gave the best ones. Early steel bands were seen as gangs and feared.

By the 1950s pans played calypso and classical music, and a band toured Britain for the Festival of Britain in 1951. The steelpan became the national instrument, at the heart of Carnival and calypso, and spread to schools around the world, carried by the diaspora.
